Species_ariados_Description: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.
Species_azumarill_Description: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.
Species_bayleef_Description: Bayleef's neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.
Species_bellossom_Description: Unlike the nocturnal Vileplume, Bellossom love to dance and bask in the warm sunlight. They often leave the forests they were born in to search for groups of other Bellossom to dance and frolic with. Gloom with particularly wretched odors have been noted to evolve into Bellossom with more vibrant and lustrous flowers.
Species_blissey_Description: A kindhearted Pokémon that will care for any sick person or Pokémon until their health improves. The eggs it lays are delicious and bring good fortune to those who eat them.
Species_celebi_Description: This Pokémon traveled through time to come from the future. It bolsters grass and trees with its own strength, and it can heal wounds, too.
Species_chikorita_Description: In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.
Species_chinchou_Description: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.
Species_cleffa_Description: In silhouette, they resemble twinkling starlight. When shooting stars rain from the night sky, Cleffa gather in numbers and dance as though they are indeed incarnations of the stars.
Species_corsola_Description: These Pokémon live in warm seas. In prehistoric times, many lived in the oceans around the Galar region as well.
Species_crobat_Description: Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.
Species_croconaw_Description: Once Croconaw has clamped its jaws on its foe, it will absolutely not let go. Because the tips of its fangs are forked back like barbed fishhooks, they become impossible to remove when they have sunk in.
Species_cyndaquil_Description: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.
Species_delibird_Description: It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it's always scrounging around for more food.
Species_donphan_Description: The larger this Pokémon's tusks are, the more respect it is given by other Donphan. When provoked, it can use these tusks to deliver blows that can easily demolish houses. However, if it's particularly enraged, it will roll up into a ball and launch itself at its foe. Occasionally, this will cause one of its tusks to come loose and fall off. Fortunately, Donphan's tusks regrow over time, and they have a variety of construction applications when collected.
Species_dunsparce_Description: The nests Dunsparce live in are mazes of tunnels. They never get lost in their own nests—they can tell where they are by the scent of the dirt.
Species_elekid_Description: They generate electricity by spinning their arms. During a thunderstorm, if one hears the lively voices of children out in the wilderness, what one is actually hearing are the voices of Elekid.
Species_entei_Description: Entei embodies the passion of magma. This Pokémon is thought to have been born in the eruption of a volcano. It sends up massive bursts of fire that utterly consume all that they touch.
Species_espeon_Description: Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.
Species_feraligatr_Description: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.
Species_flaaffy_Description: Flaaffy's skin has grown thick and rubbery to insulate it from its own electrical discharge. Its wool is much more sparse than that of Mareep, but the static electricity it builds up is much more powerful, making it dangerous to handle. As well, it is now notably more clever than Mareep, using the light on its tail to guide its flock.
Species_forretress_Description: In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.
Species_furret_Description: Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.
Species_girafarig_Description: Girafarig's rear head contains a tiny brain that is too small for thinking. However, the rear head doesn't need to sleep, so it can keep watch over its surroundings 24 hours a day.
Species_gligar_Description: Its tail is tipped by a thick, horrible stinger. To bring down prey, it will first obscure their vision by covering their faces with its body, and then it will use the stinger to inject them with venom.
Species_granbull_Description: Although it's popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it's totally incompetent as a watchdog.
Species_heracross_Description: Male specimens often dispute with each other over territory or potential mates. These disputes are settled by a direct clash of horns, hands, strength, and technique; the moment one is flipped onto its back, the conflict is decided. Despite this occasional rivalry, Heracross are generally peaceful, and they even use their horns to protect other Bug Pokémon from predators. The ones under their guard often establish a symbiotic relationship with them, repaying their protection by offering Heracross some honey, their favorite treat.
Species_hitmontop_Description: After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent's timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.
Species_ho-oh_Description: Ho-Oh's feathers glow in seven colors depending on the angle at which they are struck by light. These feathers are said to bring happiness to the bearers. This Pokémon is said to live at the foot of a rainbow.
Species_hoothoot_Description: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.
Species_hoppip_Description: This Pokémon drifts and floats with the wind. If it senses the approach of strong winds, Hoppip links its leaves with other Hoppip to prepare against being blown away.
Species_houndoom_Description: Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.
Species_houndour_Description: They make repeated eerie howls before dawn to call attention to their pack.
Species_igglybuff_Description: Taking advantage of the softness of its body, Igglybuff moves as if bouncing. Its body turns a deep pink when its temperature rises.
Species_jumpluff_Description: Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.
Species_kingdra_Description: According to legends, only Seadra that have lived a hundred years can evolve into the powerful Kingdra. Although it is capable of besting almost any foe, it spends its time in solitude in the deepest parts of the ocean. It can control the ocean currents at a whim, and sailors make offerings to it before long voyages.
Species_lanturn_Description: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.
Species_larvitar_Description: It feeds on soil. After it has eaten a large mountain, it will fall asleep so it can grow.
Species_ledian_Description: It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.
Species_ledyba_Description: These very cowardly Pokémon join together and use Reflect to protect their nest.
Species_lugia_Description: Lugia's wings pack devastating power—a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart regular houses. As a result, this Pokémon chooses to live out of sight deep under the sea.
Species_magby_Description: This Pokémon lives in volcanic areas. With each breath, sparks spurt from its mouth and nose. When Magby is in good health, its flames gain a yellow tint.
Species_magcargo_Description: Magcargo’s "shell" is actually part of its body that has solidified into brittle stone. It uses this rocky armor to defend itself, though large chunks often break off during battles. However, this doesn’t bother Magcargo—after battle it simply bathes in molten magma to regenerate its protective shell..
Species_mantine_Description: This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.
Species_mareep_Description: This common Pokémon is often found grazing in fields and meadows. Mareep regrows its coat quickly when shorn, making it a useful source of wool. It uses this wool to build up small amounts of static electricity for its tail, which it uses to communicate with other Mareep.
Species_marill_Description: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water- repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That's why this Pokémon is never cold.
Species_meganium_Description: The fragrance of Meganium's flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe's fighting spirit.
Species_miltank_Description: A healthy Miltank can easily produce multiple buckets of milk in a day. This Pokémon is a favorite among alchemists and explorers, as its nutritious milk can nullify the adverse effects of any nasty potion they may encounter. Miltank is especially popular with adventurous types, as it packs more punch than it may seem. With a single Rollout attack, it can turn fallen debris into splinters, clearing the path forwards.
Species_misdreavus_Description: Misdreavus loves to frighten children by releasing blood-curdling shrieks and sobs into the dead of night, feasting on the fear it creates by doing so. Its hauntings have become so frequent that some people even report seeing its eerie hair in their nightmares.
Species_murkrow_Description: Widely shunned as a bearer of ill fortune. Upon crossing paths with this creature, I've been told one must chant ”Workrum, Workrum—bad luck, don't come” as a protective incantation.
Species_natu_Description: Natu's wings aren't yet developed enough for it to fly, so it wanders under trees where other Pokémon live, hoping that their movement will cause fruit to fall for it to eat. Although this position puts it at risk of being confronted by ground predators, it has quite an effective trick for warding off enemies; its eerie gaze. Anything that locks eyes with Natu is overcome with an intense feeling of dread and anxiety, often causing them to flee.
Species_noctowl_Description: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.
Species_octillery_Description: While Octillery still shoots water from its mouth, the drastic anatomical difference between it and Remoraid meant that for a long time, no one believed the former evolved from the latter.
Species_phanpy_Description: Phanpy use their extremely dexterous trunks for nearly everything, from expressing emotions to washing themselves. Groups of Phanpy can be found near shallow ponds, spraying each other with the water gathered in their trunks and playing in the mud. Unfortunately, they're much stronger than they appear. When overwhelmed with joy, their reckless flailing will knock back anything that gets too close.
Species_pichu_Description: While Pichu are in possession of impressive electrical power, they have yet to learn how to control it and tend to shock themselves as much as their opponents. Interestingly, groups of Pichu have been seen intentionally triggering these discharges by touching tails, creating a shower of sparks in the process. Researchers believe this is an attempt to gain more mastery over their abilities.
Species_piloswine_Description: The long fur of this Pokémon covers its eyes, ears, and even limbs, allowing Piloswine to resist harshly frigid conditions. The Pokémon's white tusks can be used to defeat its enemies.
Species_pineco_Description: It sticks tree bark to itself with its saliva, making itself thicker and larger. Elderly Pineco are ridiculously huge.
Species_politoed_Description: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.
Species_porygon2_Description: With its evolution induced by an object of equal curiosity, Porygon2 seems more... realistic than its predecesor? Certainly the rough edges have been polished, and it seems to display higher levels of conciousness and mobility. Still, it has no need for food or breath, and the prospect of using it to explore previously unreachable domains is alluring. Perhaps one more "upgrade" will do?
Species_pupitar_Description: It will not stay still, even while it's a pupa. It already has arms and legs under its solid shell.
Species_quagsire_Description: Quagsire often find themselves tangled within the twisting roots of mangrove trees as they swim, but thanks to their absentminded personalities, they don't thrash or struggle. Instead, they're able to calmly slip their slimy bodies through the roots. In fact, this Pokémon is so aloof that it is completely oblivious to others riding on its back, but it is nonetheless happy to transport these friends across shallow waters.
Species_quilava_Description: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.
Species_qwilfish_Description: These spiny Pokémon are found in warm waters, armed with dangerous venom spines that they can fire like arrows to dissuade any would-be predators. They are often found in and around Ocean Monuments, and are notably unbothered by Guardians. This could perhaps be due to similarities in their behavior and physiology.
Species_raikou_Description: Raikou embodies the speed of lightning. The roars of this Pokémon send shock waves shuddering through the air and shake the ground as if lightning bolts had come crashing down.
Species_remoraid_Description: Spits water from its mouth with incredible accuracy. It captures Burmy by shooting them down off the branches from which they dangle.
Species_scizor_Description: Evolved by way of a curious item. The shell covering its body has been shown to be stronger than forged steel.
Species_sentret_Description: When Sentret sleeps, it does so while another stands guard. The sentry wakes the others at the first sign of danger. When this Pokémon becomes separated from its pack, it becomes incapable of sleep due to fear.
Species_shuckle_Description: When threatened, Shuckle hides beneath rocks and remains completely still, capable of surviving for years without eating. Inside its shell, natural processes allow it to ferment and recycle food efficiently, producing a berry juice believed to boost vitality and cure ailments. As Shuckle ages, its shell grows stronger, leading to tales of ancient Shuckle whose shells became nearly impenetrable.
Species_skarmory_Description: People fashion swords from Skarmory's shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.
Species_skiploom_Description: Skiploom's flower blossoms when the temperature rises above 64 degrees Fahrenheit. How much the flower opens depends on the temperature. For that reason, this Pokémon is sometimes used as a thermometer.
Species_slowking_Description: Slowking receives a stimulant injected directly into its brain by the Shellder clamped onto its head, resulting in a remarkable boost in intellect and intuition. Some Slowbro even gather to follow it as servants, drawn by its cool confidence and strategic wisdom in difficult situations. The only thing that disrupts its composure is losing an intellectual challenge—a rare occurrence, of course.
Species_slugma_Description: The thick gel that makes up Slugma’s body is similar to magma cream, allowing it to maintain its molten form and incredibly high body temperatures. Slugma can only survive near intense heat sources, like the vast, burning seas of the Nether, as its body quickly solidifies in cooler environments.
Species_smeargle_Description: It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.
Species_smoochum_Description: This is a very curious Pokémon. Smoochum decides what it likes and dislikes by touching things with its lips.
Species_sneasel_Description: A sly Pokémon that lives off ill-gotten gains, Sneasel uses its sharp, curved claws to access nests high in trees or just beneath the soil. Often working in pairs, one Sneasel lures a Pokémon from its nest while the other snatches anything it deems valuable. It's not uncommon for Sneasel to steal food, shiny objects, or other treasures, making it a master of mischief
Species_snubbull_Description: In contrast to its appearance, it's quite timid. When playing with other puppy Pokémon, it sometimes gets bullied.
Species_spinarak_Description: Although the poison from its fangs isn't that strong, it's potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.
Species_stantler_Description: Ancient records suggest that Stantler once possessed great psychic powers, but the absence of predators in its habitat led to these abilities being neglected and ultimately lost. However, a remnant of its past self lingers, particularly in its antlers. Gazing at them induces hypnotic sensations, capable of locking a victim's gaze until they faint. Contrary to popular belief, this effect is activated consciously, meaning the species is not as defenseless as many have speculated.
Species_steelix_Description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a strange item. Its body is coated with steel powder and notably hard—not even diamond can leave so much as a scratch.
Species_sudowoodo_Description: A cunning Pokémon that mimics a tree, despite being comprised of a more rock-like substance. Due to its Rock-typing, this behavior is theorized to exist to dissuade Water-types and lure in Bug-types for advantageous battles. The only flaw in Sudowoodo's master plan is its weakness to water. If any generous trainer approaches it with a watering can in hand, it will immediately abandon its masquerade and flee.
Species_suicune_Description: Suicune embodies the compassion of a pure spring of water. It runs across the land with gracefulness. This Pokémon has the power to purify dirty water.
Species_sunflora_Description: Like many Grass-type Pokémon, Sunflora generates energy through photosynthesis, converting sunlight into nutrients. Throughout the day, it energetically rushes from place to place, fanning its petals and leaves in hopes to absorb as much sunlight as possible. When night falls, Sunflora stops moving entirely, conserving the nutrients it's created. These behaviors make it highly efficient at gathering and storing solar energy.
Species_sunkern_Description: Sunkern subsists on morning dewdrops that form on low-lying foliage. To conserve energy until its evolution, it moves very little and relies on a unique defense: if threatened, this fragile Pokémon will shake violently in hopes of scaring off attackers. Its bright, summery yellow hue is thought to be the origin of an old wives' tale, claiming that newborn Sunkern fall from the sky like drops of sunshine.
Species_swinub_Description: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.
Species_teddiursa_Description: It licks its paws because of the sweet honey that has soaked into them. It is cunning, stealing into the nests of Combee and taking for itself the honey that the Combee have amassed.
Species_togepi_Description: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.
Species_togetic_Description: No records exist of Togetic being seen in the wilds. Rumors abound that it evolves under the loving care of a trusted human companion, upon whom the Pokémon then bestows great joy.
Species_totodile_Description: Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile's jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.
Species_typhlosion_Description: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.
Species_tyranitar_Description: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.
Species_tyrogue_Description: Even though it is small, it can't be ignored because it will slug any handy target without warning.
Species_umbreon_Description: It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.
Species_unown_Description: It is hard to believe these strangely shaped Pokémon are truly living creatures. I've pointed out that the species' many forms resemble writing from other lands; no one will take me seriously.
Species_ursaring_Description: When the cold season arrives in Hisui, this Pokémon will wander fields and mountains alike in search of its favorite berries. Ursaring's hunger during this time makes it a ferocious danger.
Species_wobbuffet_Description: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.
Species_wooper_Description: This playful Pokémon enjoys splashing around in the muddy waters of its habitat, sociable to not only its own kind but to other Pokémon and humans as well. Unfortunately, it doesn't know that the membrane that keeps its body moist on land contains a weak numbing toxin. If you pat a Wooper on the head, you may be unable to feel your hand for the next few hours.
Species_xatu_Description: Aside from its eyes restlessly following the sun, Xatu stands motionless for most of the day. Some "theorists" postulate that this activity is what gives Xatu its precognition. They claim that the sun shares its knowledge of the future with Xatu, and that its emotionless expression is due to how macabre the fate of our world appears to be. Many attempts have been made to discover the secrets seen by this mysterious Pokémon, but no matter the strength of the psychic, its mind seems impenetrable.
Species_yanma_Description: Its frail wings are so thin that one can see clear through them. However, during flight these wings exhibit the power to churn air with force enough to launch a house skyward.
Species_absol_Description: Because of this Pokémon's ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.
Species_aggron_Description: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon's strength.
Species_altaria_Description: This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it's provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.
Species_anorith_Description: Anorith can swim swiftly by pulling its eight wings through the water like oars on a boat. This Pokémon is an ancestor of modern bug Pokémon.
Species_armaldo_Description: Though it lives on land, it's also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.
Species_aron_Description: When Aron evolves, its steel armor peels off. In ancient times, people would collect Aron's shed armor and make good use of it in their daily lives.
Species_azurill_Description: Although Azurill are normally docile, an angry one will swing around the big ball on its tail and try to smash its opponents.
Species_bagon_Description: Bagon is a solitary Pokémon that doesn't form groups with others of its kind. It also has a head hard enough to cleave a boulder in one strike.
Species_baltoy_Description: Illustrations found in millenia-old ruins almost always depict Baltoy interacting with humans, and especially children. Because it moves by spinning around on a single foot, it's theorized that children would play with this Pokémon as if it were a top..
Species_banette_Description: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.
Species_barboach_Description: Makes its home in swamps with murky water. The poor visibility hides this Pokémon from predators, and the slime on its body makes grasping it difficult.
Species_beautifly_Description: A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.
Species_beldum_Description: The cells in this Pokémon's body are composed of magnetic material. Instead of blood, magnetic forces flow through Beldum's body.
Species_blaziken_Description: Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon's blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.
Species_breloom_Description: When it or its kin are threatened, Breloom uses the toxic seeds on its tail to incapacitate would-be attackers. While its foes are stunned, it throws punches with its stretchy arms that would put professional boxers to shame. In the wild, it uses these punches to knock berries out of trees for itself and its kin to eat.
Species_cacnea_Description: The more arid and harsh the environment, the more pretty and fragrant a flower Cacnea grows. This Pokémon battles by wildly swinging its thorny arms.
Species_cacturne_Description: If a traveler is going through a desert in the thick of night, Cacturne will follow in a ragtag group. The Pokémon are biding their time, waiting for the traveler to tire and become incapable of moving.
Species_camerupt_Description: The pressure within its lava-storing humps is now so great that it is constantly at risk of erupting. However, with careful harvesting, this lava can be extracted and used in metallurgy, making Camerupt a popular Pokémon among blacksmiths. When in need of a refuel, it eats rocks and ore, melting them down using its own body heat.
Species_carvanha_Description: Despite this voracious Pokémon's aggressive mentality, Carvanha refuses to attack an enemy alone. It will sit and wait silently for other members of its pack to arrive, where they will proceed to mercilessly tear into their target with red, jagged fangs. While isolated individuals of this species are rather timid, packs of Carvanha will attack anything that touches the water, seemingly without any provocation. Most seasoned fishermen know to cover their wounds before setting sail, as even a single drop of blood will send a pack of Carvanha into a boat-splintering frenzy.
Species_cascoon_Description: The silk coating its body is thin but sufficiently strong. Cascoon's silk has a luster and texture superior to that of Silcoon's, and clothes made using Cascoon silk are regarded as top-notch.
Species_castform_Description: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform's disposition!
Species_chimecho_Description: Can emit waves of air powerful enough to knock out prey taller than itself. I hypothesize that it amplifies the faint sound of wind within its body.
Species_clamperl_Description: This Pokémon's beautiful pearl is protected by its rock-solid shell, which shrugs off bites even from predators as ferocious as Sharpedo. Clamperl is usually a filter feeder sustained by marine snow, but a particularly hungry specimen may clamp down onto a passing Drowned, latching on for a hearty, rotting, meal.
Species_claydol_Description: The art on Claydol's body bears heavy remblance to pottery sherds found buried under grand temples in the desert. It's unclear what relation they have to the structure or the ancient civilization that build it, but they can still be found wandering near them to this day.
Species_combusken_Description: Combusken battles with the intensely hot flames it spews from its beak and with outstandingly destructive kicks. This Pokémon's cry is very loud and distracting.
Species_corphish_Description: It was originally a Pokémon from afar that escaped to the wild. It can adapt to the dirtiest river.
Species_cradily_Description: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.
Species_crawdaunt_Description: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.
Species_delcatty_Description: Delcatty sleeps anywhere it wants without keeping a permanent nest. If other Pokémon approach it as it sleeps, this Pokémon will never fight—it will just move away somewhere else.
Species_deoxys_Description: Deoxys emerged from a virus that came from space. It is highly intelligent and wields psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon shoots lasers from the crystalline organ on its chest.
Species_dusclops_Description: There aren't many studies around this Pokémon's body, as it is capable of absorbing almost anything that strays too close. Although Dusclops mostly uses this skill as a defense and hunting mechanism, it is also believed that it consumes random pieces of buildings or land, simply because it finds it funny to leave them incomplete.
Species_duskull_Description: Duskull's body is only semi-corporeal, allowing it to pass through any object, regardless of composition or size. It uses this ability to stay inside walls and observe prey, planning the best strategy to carry out an ambush. As it stalks through the night in search of prey, it can't help but be drawn to the cries of misbehaving children.
Species_dustox_Description: Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.
Species_electrike_Description: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.
Species_exploud_Description: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it'll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.
Species_feebas_Description: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.
Species_flygon_Description: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.
Species_gardevoir_Description: Gardevoir is fiercely loyal and dedicated to protecting its Trainer, having been in sync with their emotions for so long. Should one it cares about fall in battle, Gardevoir's emotions become too much for it to bear. In a fit of rage and grief, it can expend all of its psychic energy to tear a pitch-dark hole through the dimensions. No creature - human, Pokémon, or otherwise - on the receiving end of this devastating attack has ever been found afterwards.
Species_glalie_Description: It covers its body with an armor of ice harder than steel. Uses its breath to freeze prey, which it then devours as if they were frozen desserts.
Species_gorebyss_Description: Exposure to a thalassic Pokémon's beautiful scale has caused Clamperl to evolve into this form. Gorebyss has elegant, tough scales, but is surprisingly aggressive. It uses its strong fins and sharp beak to forcefully jab through anything that could potentially make for a good meal. Although it rarely comes up to the surface, sailors take great caution in waters inhabited by these Pokémon, as they often mistake boats for large prey and can cause serious damage to the hull.
Species_groudon_Description: Through Primal Reversion and with nature's full power, it will take back its true form. It can cause magma to erupt and expand the landmass of the world.
Species_grovyle_Description: This Pokémon adeptly flies from branch to branch in trees. In a forest, no Pokémon can ever hope to catch a fleeing Grovyle however fast they may be.
Species_grumpig_Description: Grumpig uses the black pearls on its body to wield its fantastic powers. When it is doing so, it dances bizarrely. This Pokémon's black pearls are valuable as works of art.
Species_gulpin_Description: Most of Gulpin's body is made up of its stomach—its heart and brain are very small in comparison. This Pokémon's stomach contains special enzymes that dissolve anything.
Species_hariyama_Description: Hariyama that are big and fat aren't necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.
Species_huntail_Description: Exposure to a thalassic Pokémon's sharp tooth has caused Clamperl to evolve into this form. Huntail has an incredibly powerful jaw, but is far from a mindless hunter, using its bio-luminescent spots and fish-shaped tail to lure in prey before biting down with steel-crushing pressure. Its mouth can open wide enough to take huge bites out of prey larger than itself, and has even been seen devouring whole schools of smaller fish in a single bite.n.
Species_illumise_Description: Illumise leads a flight of illuminated Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. This Pokémon is said to earn greater respect from its peers by composing more complex designs in the sky.
Species_jirachi_Description: It's believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.
Species_kecleon_Description: Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.
Species_kirlia_Description: Exposure to high amounts of positive emotion has heightened Kirlia's psychokinetic power. With a quick spin and a single dance, this Pokémon can create mirages of far-off paradises and peer into the future. Its connection to emotion was once a liability as a Ralts, but after honing its psychic capabilities, almost any emotion causes its power to grow.
Species_kyogre_Description: Kyogre is said to be the personification of the sea itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Groudon, as each sought to gain the power of nature.
Species_lairon_Description: During territorial disputes, Lairon fight by slamming into each other. Close inspection of their steel armor reveals scratches and dents.
Species_latias_Description: Latias is highly intelligent and capable of understanding human speech. It is covered with a glass-like down. The Pokémon enfolds its body with its down and refracts light to alter its appearance.
Species_latios_Description: Latios will only open its heart to a Trainer with a compassionate spirit. This Pokémon can fly faster than a jet plane by folding its forelegs to minimize air resistance.
Species_lileep_Description: Lileep clings to rocks on the seabed. When prey comes close, this Pokémon entangles it with petallike tentacles.
Species_linoone_Description: It uses its explosive speed and razor-sharp claws to bring down prey. Running along winding paths is not its strong suit.
Species_lombre_Description: It lives at the water's edge where it is sunny. It sleeps on a bed of water grass by day and becomes active at night.
Species_lotad_Description: Its leaf grew too large for it to live on land. That is how it began to live floating in the water.
Species_loudred_Description: The force of this Pokémon's loud voice isn't just the sound—it's also the wave of air pressure that blows opponents away and damages them.
Species_ludicolo_Description: If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.
Species_lunatone_Description: It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.
Species_luvdisc_Description: These shallow-swimming Pokémon are known for their strong social bonds, and they become despondent when separated from their companion. Once one finds a mate, they will stay together for their entire lives, leading to Luvdisc being seen as a symbol of everlasting love in many cultures. These Pokémon are often found making their nests among the branches of Corsola, keeping a lookout for predators whilst gaining the benefit of a secure and mobile home.
Species_makuhita_Description: There's a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.
Species_manectric_Description: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.
Species_marshtomp_Description: Marshtomp is much faster at traveling through mud than it is at swimming. This Pokémon's hindquarters exhibit obvious development, giving it the ability to walk on just its hind legs.
Species_masquerain_Description: Masquerain are highly sensitive to the water quality and overall health of their environment, even to the point of chasing off potential polluters. Because of this, ecologists will often observe Masquerain to monitor the health of an ecosystem. If their population is high, there's nothing to worry about.
Species_mawile_Description: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.
Species_medicham_Description: Through the power of meditation, Medicham developed its sixth sense. It gained the ability to use psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon is known to meditate for a whole month without eating.
Species_meditite_Description: Meditite heightens its inner energy through meditation. It survives on just one berry a day. Minimal eating is another aspect of this Pokémon's training.
Species_metagross_Description: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.
Species_metang_Description: Using magnetic forces to stay aloft, this Pokémon flies at high speeds, weaving through harsh mountain terrain in pursuit of prey.
Species_mightyena_Description: Mightyena travel and act as a pack in the wild. The memory of its life in the wild compels the Pokémon to obey only those Trainers that it recognizes to possess superior skill.
Species_milotic_Description: It's said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you're feeling.
Species_minun_Description: Minun loves to cheer on its partner in battle. It gives off sparks from its body while it is doing so. If its partner is in trouble, this Pokémon gives off increasing amounts of sparks.
Species_mudkip_Description: In water, Mudkip breathes using the gills on its cheeks. If it is faced with a tight situation in battle, this Pokémon will unleash its amazing power—it can crush rocks bigger than itself.
Species_nincada_Description: Nincada spends most of its time underground, remaining almost entirely still as it waits for the moment to evolve. It thrives in the cool, damp earth, away from harsh weather that its delicate body cannot withstand. While awake, it uses its sharp claws to dig into tree roots, absorbing moisture and nutrients. However, its solitary existence leaves it vulnerable to subterranean predators, who can easily breach its insect shell defenses.
Species_ninjask_Description: Ninjask possesses the highest speeds ever seen in an ordinary Pokémon, sometimes moving so fast it becomes invisible. It only slows down when it's feeding on tree sap, which predators use as an opportunity to strike. However, its reaction speed is equally remarkable; the moment danger reveals itself, it hastily darts away. Some even retaliate by emitting a piercing cry that can induce severe headaches in their attackers.
Species_nosepass_Description: With incredibly precise magnetic senses, Nosepass instinctively direct themselves towards a specific geographic location. While the reason behind this behavior remains shrouded in mystery, travelers often use Nosepass as a guide on long journeys. However, if a Nosepass finds itself in another dimension, it will become dazed and disoriented, unable to determine its own location.ses.
Species_numel_Description: Numel are exceptionally hardy Pokémon found in hot, dry areas. They have even been observed herding within the wastes of the Nether, gulping down buckets worth of lava at a time to store within their humps. They are incredibly dull-witted, and it can take them several moments to even notice that they are being attacked.
Species_nuzleaf_Description: They live in holes bored in large trees. The sound of Nuzleaf's grass flute fills listeners with dread.
Species_pelipper_Description: Skimming the water's surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.
Species_plusle_Description: When Plusle is cheering on its partner, it flashes with electric sparks from all over its body. If its partner loses, this Pokémon cries loudly.
Species_poochyena_Description: Poochyena is an omnivore—it will eat anything. A distinguishing feature is how large its fangs are compared to its body. This Pokémon tries to intimidate its foes by making the hair on its tail bristle out.
Species_ralts_Description: The horn on its head is able to attune itself to the emotions of humans around it, but Ralts has yet to learn how to control this ability. As a result, it unintentionally reflects and amplifies these emotions; if it's around happy people, Ralts will be joyous, but if it's around gloomy people, it will become miserable. Because of this, it will often hide away from humans, only approaching if it senses positivity.
Species_rayquaza_Description: It flies forever through the ozone layer, consuming meteoroids for sustenance. The many meteoroids in its body provide the energy it needs to Mega Evolve.
Species_regice_Description: This Pokémon's body is made of solid ice. It's said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.
Species_regirock_Description: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon's rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.
Species_registeel_Description: It's rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet's mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.
Species_relicanth_Description: Comparisons between old records and living individuals show that this Pokémon has existed unchanged for countless generations. At one point, Relicanth was thought to be extinct, but the recent sighting of a specimen inside a deep ocean trench put an end to that possibility. Its rock-hard scales and unique method of swimming allows it to resist the pressure of this environment, but the purpose of the twin red markings on its body is unknown. Legends suggest that these serve as a map to "long-lost giants," but what that means, if anything at all, is still undiscovered.
Species_roselia_Description: Though beautiful, it has highly poisonous thorns. There is an old tradition in my homeland wherein one would send these thorns to an opponent to challenge them to a duel.
Species_sableye_Description: Sableye can often be found in underground geodes to satiate their unusual diet of minerals, this strange eating habit results in their own bodies being partially comprised of gemstones, with their apparent preference for amethyst in particular contributing to their purple color. Sableye will often fight each other for dibs on the largest clusters in a geode, however, even the most territorial of Sableye will abandon everything if they spot their favorite prey - Carbink.
Species_salamence_Description: While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.
Species_sceptile_Description: Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.
Species_sealeo_Description: Its white whiskers are very sensitive. Sealeo will balance Spheal on the tip of its nose, checking its scent and its feel to be sure the Spheal is healthy.
Species_seedot_Description: It attaches itself to a tree branch using the top of its head. Strong winds can sometimes make it fall.
Species_seviper_Description: Seviper's swordlike tail serves two purposes—it slashes foes and douses them with secreted poison. This Pokémon will not give up its long-running blood feud with Zangoose.
Species_sharpedo_Description: Sharpedo's specialized skin helps it swim at outstanding speeds, allowing it to perform almost instantaneous onslaughts. This brutal aquatic predator is known as the "Bully of the Sea," a nickname it earned with its insatiable appetite for brutality. Oftentimes, it will attack stone or metal simply because it craves violence, causing its teeth to chip and shatter. Although, its teeth grow back rapidly, allowing it to continue non-stop on its lifelong rampage. Any life in the sea could be its next target; fish, other Pokémon, Drowned, and even living humans.
Species_shedinja_Description: After a Nincada evolves, its discarded carapace can sometimes take on a life of its own. Shedinja’s eerie stillness stands in contrast to Ninjask’s vibrant energy. This empty shell remains completely motionless, without a single twitch, and it’s unclear whether it has any will or consciousness. It doesn’t react to stimuli and seems devoid of emotions. Those who peer into its hollow back often begin to exhibit similar signs of lifelessness.
Species_shelgon_Description: Shelgon ignores its hunger entirely, never eating any food. Apparently, Shelgon will evolve once all its energy stores are used up.
Species_shiftry_Description: It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.
Species_shroomish_Description: Shroomish prefer dark, damp places, and they will sleep through the daylight hidden under forest trees or fallen leaves. Once the sun sets, they love to roam around and munch away at rotting leaves and decaying debris. When threatened, they become very anxious, and without warning, they will let out a burst of toxic spores from the bud at the top of their head.
Species_shuppet_Description: There's a proverb that says, “Shun the house where Shuppet gather in the growing dusk.”
Species_silcoon_Description: Wraps itself in thin strings of silk while it stores energy for evolution. It can't extend its limbs and its movement is slow, but its eyes keep a sharp lookout—Silcoon is always on guard.
Species_skitty_Description: Skitty is known to chase around playfully after its own tail. In the wild, this Pokémon lives in holes in the trees of forests. It is very popular as a pet because of its adorable looks.
Species_slaking_Description: Wherever Slaking live, rings of over a yard in diameter appear in grassy fields. They are made by the Pokémon as it eats all the grass within reach while lying prone on the ground.
Species_slakoth_Description: Slakoth's heart beats just once a minute. Whatever happens, it is content to loaf around motionless. It is rare to see this Pokémon in motion.
Species_snorunt_Description: Arrives alongside the first snow. It's thought that homes Snorunt visit will prosper for many generations. By tradition, one might offer a lump of ice made from pure water at one's front door.
Species_solrock_Description: Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.
Species_spheal_Description: During the season when drift ice approaches the shore, Spheal prefers living on the ice—where fewer predators lurk—rather than the land. Its fur retains heat superbly and resists harsh cold.
Species_spinda_Description: Though their sporadic movements seem random, some claim that Spinda follow a mysterious and mesmerizing choreography. They are known to perform in the strangest places, even on the roofs of buildings or down in lost caverns, with no clear explanation of how they got there. Each Spinda has a wholly unique pattern of spots that cause their opponents to become confused when paired with their teetering pirouettes and unsteady steps. Interestingly, clothing mimicking Spinda spots appear to cause trainers to become harder to track, much like the Pokémon itself.!
Species_spoink_Description: Spoink keeps a pearl on top of its head. The pearl functions to amplify this Pokémon's psychokinetic powers. It is therefore on a constant search for a bigger pearl.
Species_surskit_Description: Wild Surskit usually hold a diet of whatever detritus floats on top of their ponds. However, if one is desperate enough for food, it'll seek out groups of other Surskit to drink the sticky-sweet syrup they produce from the tips of their heads.
Species_swablu_Description: Since Swablu looks like a cumulus cloud, foes can have a hard time finding it. Apparently its wings turned white over many generations.
Species_swalot_Description: Swalot has no teeth, so what it eats, it swallows whole, no matter what. Its cavernous mouth yawns widely. An automobile tire could easily fit inside this Pokémon's mouth.
Species_swampert_Description: Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.
Species_swellow_Description: Swellow is very conscientious about the upkeep of its glossy wings. Once two Swellow are gathered, they diligently take care of cleaning each other's wings.
Species_taillow_Description: Taillow is young—it has only just left its nest. As a result, it sometimes becomes lonesome and cries at night. This Pokémon feeds on Wurmple that live in forests.
Species_torchic_Description: Torchic has a place inside its body where it keeps its flame. Give it a hug—it will be glowing with warmth. This Pokémon is covered all over by a fluffy coat of down.
Species_torkoal_Description: Although coal is the most plentiful mineral in the world, there is always a notable decline in its concentration around areas where Torkoal lives. This smoky Pokémon digs up the ore in mass amounts, which it burns inside its shell to provide its body with energy. This process releases thick billows of smoke, which it uses as a distraction against other Pokémon. While this intense volume of soot and vapor is irritating to most people, it seems that Torkoal loves it, maintaining a calm and serene expression when surrounded by its own smog..
Species_trapinch_Description: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.
Species_treecko_Description: Treecko is cool, calm, and collected—it never panics under any situation. If a bigger foe were to glare at this Pokémon, it would glare right back without conceding an inch of ground.
Species_tropius_Description: Fossil records indicate that this gentle giant has been roaming the jungle, both on foot and in flight, since ancient times. The fruit that grows on Tropius's neck is sweet and nutritious, and it is enjoyed by people and Pokémon alike. As the berries ripen, people gather around it to feed on them. Tropius doesn't mind this at all, as sharing its fruit helps to spread its seeds.
Species_vibrava_Description: To help make its wings grow, it dissolves quantities of prey in its digestive juices and guzzles them down every day.
Species_vigoroth_Description: Vigoroth is simply incapable of remaining still. Even when it tries to sleep, the blood in its veins grows agitated, compelling this Pokémon to run wild throughout the jungle before it can settle down.
Species_volbeat_Description: Volbeat's tail glows like a lightbulb. With other Volbeat, it uses its tail to draw geometric shapes in the night sky. This Pokémon loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.
Species_wailmer_Description: Although these Pokémon are primarily aquatic, they occasionally gather in large groups on beaches. Having filled themselves with seawater, they bounce playfully across the sand. However, Wailmer are not very skilled at controlling their bounce, and they often end up tumbling into others of their kind. This doesn’t seem to bother them though, as they are protected by a thick layer of blubber.
Species_wailord_Description: Few predators can hope to threaten this massive Pokémon, so it spends its life floating calmly beneath the waves, opening its cavernous mouth to swallow up schools of smaller Pokémon and plant debris. Wailord’s body is full of air, so it takes a lot of energy for it to stay underwater. When it's ready to return from the depths, it uses its natural buoyancy to rocket upwards, breaching the surface at incredible speeds..
Species_walrein_Description: Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.
Species_whiscash_Description: Strikes its caudal fin against the swamp bed to shake the ground and startle its prey. It will then swallow the fleeing prey whole. People mistook this behavior as the cause of earthquakes.
Species_whismur_Description: When Whismur cries, the sound of its own voice startles it, making the Pokémon cry even louder. It cries until it's exhausted, then it falls asleep.
Species_wingull_Description: It soars on updrafts without flapping its wings. It makes a nest on sheer cliffs at the sea's edge.
Species_wurmple_Description: Likes sap and is abundant in the wild. Why it evolves into various different forms is unknown. One cannot tell from a Wurmple's appearance which form it will take when it evolves.
Species_wynaut_Description: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.
Species_zangoose_Description: Zangoose usually stays on all fours, but when angered, it gets up on its hind legs and extends its claws. This Pokémon shares a bitter rivalry with Seviper that dates back over generations.
Species_zigzagoon_Description: Zigzagoon that adapted to regions outside Galar acquired this appearance. If you've lost something, this Pokémon can likely find it.
Species_abomasnow_Description: A powerful Pokémon that can split huge boulders with ease. Dislikes associating with others and chooses to live quietly deep within the mountains, playing with the snow.
Species_ambipom_Description: As a sign of camaraderie, these sociable Pokémon perform an intricate dance with their twin tails. This showcase can often lead to the creation of treetop colonies, where groups of Ambipom that are especially close will venture out to find food. On these expeditions, the sight of a Primeape is a common event. While these natural rivals may have the upper hand with typing, they certainly don't possess the intelligence advantage. The clever groups of Ambipom will make upsetting gestures with their hands to distract Primeape from the real danger: their tails.
Species_arceus_Description: It is the heavenly fount from which pours the light that shines across Hisui. Its luminance guides and protects all Pokémon. Hisuian mythology states that Arceus is the creator of all things.
Species_azelf_Description: The dreaded Being of Willpower. Legends tell of this Pokémon manipulating the will of its adversaries and turning them into puppets of its own.
Species_bastiodon_Description: Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.
Species_bibarel_Description: Bibarel fur repels water and is also a fantastic material for heat retention. These Pokémon create dams on rivers to live in.
Species_bidoof_Description: Bidoof has an unsophisticated face and is rarely flustered by anything. There have been incidents involving Bidoof sauntering into villages and gnawing on the houses without a single care.
Species_bonsly_Description: Living in arid environments, Bonsly releases excess moisture through its eyes, in a manner similar to sweating. Because this looks like crying, many Pokémon prefer not to attack it out of sympathy. It can be often found near Sudowoodo, where it watches their mimicry to practice its own.
Species_bronzong_Description: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.
Species_bronzor_Description: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.
Species_budew_Description: When the sun's light strengthens, the bud atop this Pokémon's head opens. This is a sign to the people that the harsh winter is over, and the season of budding has begun.
Species_buizel_Description: It moves freely in the water by spinning its forked tail for propulsion. The resemblance to the screw of a steamboat is coincidental.
Species_buneary_Description: My hypothesis as to why Buneary rolls up its ears is that its hearing is far too keen. I surmise that the Pokémon protects its hearing by limiting the sound that may enter its ears.
Species_burmy_Description: If its cloak is even slightly damaged, Burmy will immediately repair it with whatever is close at hand. The Pokémon within the cloak is scrawny and vulnerable to the cold.
Species_carnivine_Description: When blended in with the vegetation remaining still, this Pokémon's camouflage is practically undetectable. Carnivine leaves its mouth agape and secretes a toxic sweet-smelling saliva to attract its prey. Once anything ventures close enough, its jaws snap shut. It grows larger every time it feeds, with no apparent upper limit. However, the larger it grows, the more lethargic and vulnerable to hunters it becomes. Rangers are frequently dispatched to help control the Carnivine population, and also to collect its saliva, which, when prepared correctly, is considered a delicacy.
Species_chatot_Description: A curious, intelligent Pokémon with a remarkably developed voice, Chatot is adept at mimicking the sounds of nature, other Pokémon, and even human speech. It uses this unusual ability to distract and confuse predators, fooling them into thinking it's something larger and more intimidating. This Pokémon also displays a strong affinity for music, often gathering around jukeboxes and swaying its tail feathers rhythmically to the beat.
Species_cherrim_Description: Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim's folded petals.
Species_cherubi_Description: Once the fruit growing alongside the main body is large and plump, Cherubi will use the nutrients within to evolve. The fruit then detaches, becoming nourishment for other creatures.
Species_chimchar_Description: Full of vigor and always in high spirits. It was once known by the name ”Lantern-Tail” and feared as some kind of apparition.
Species_chingling_Description: This Pokémon gave me an excruciating headache when it seemingly cried out without making a sound. Perhaps there are some sounds that the human ear is simply incapable of hearing.
Species_combee_Description: They swear fealty to a queen Pokémon and work diligently to gather nectar. Each swarm produces a different flavor of honey.
Species_cranidos_Description: An incredibly rare sight. They duel each other by ramming their heads together, and the resulting sound echoes throughout the area like the pealing of a bell.
Species_cresselia_Description: Cresselia is reminiscent of the crescent moon. It leaves a brilliant line of light in its wake as it flies across the night sky. I daresay it resembles the heavenly maiden who created the Milky Way.
Species_croagunk_Description: A poison wielder with a dastardly personality. Despite such qualities, this species is afforded a measure of popularity due to its peculiar cry and comical features.
Species_darkrai_Description: On a moonless night, a strange incident occurred in which every one of a village's inhabitants suffered nightmares. The villagers attested that Darkrai appeared before them in these nightmares.
Species_dialga_Description: This Pokémon is revered as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Dialga was what caused the vast river of time to begin flowing in our world.
Species_drapion_Description: Has a brutish, ferocious temperament. With immense strength and a sturdy shell off which swords will bounce, it rampages about and wreaks havoc.
Species_drifblim_Description: There are records from centuries ago that claim that this melancholic Pokémon was one of the first tested as a viable method of mass transportation. This possibility was quickly rejected, after several incidents occurred where Drifblim simply carried people up and over the horizon, never to be seen again. Even in the cases where chase was given to the fleeing abductor, they inexplicably seemed to vanish into thin air.
Species_drifloon_Description: Drifloon is known to grab children that have been left alone in the night and whisk them away, but perhaps this is a misunderstood protective behavior? Some people suggest that the souls trapped inside Drifloon are that of children's caregivers, desperate to take abandoned kids away from the dangers of the night. When this Pokémon bursts, the souls disperse. Knowing they can no longer protect children, they let out a cry of pain as they return to the land of spirits.
Species_dusknoir_Description: According to folklore, Dusknoir is believed to be a ferryman of souls to the world of spirits. Any attempts to gather readings from it are met with strange static noise, and it often prefers isolation in the wild. This obscures any understanding of if, why, or how it performs its duties as a ferryman. However, after several sightings of this enigmatic Pokémon in soul sand valleys, it raises the possibility that this might be its—and perhaps our—final destination.
Species_electivire_Description: Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.
Species_empoleon_Description: Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.
Species_finneon_Description: What a gorgeous sight this Pokémon is as it swims with its long, pink-painted caudal fins fluttering behind it. Finneon's beautiful appearance has led to its nickname: ”finery fish.”
Species_floatzel_Description: Has a long, rather splendid flotation sac, which prevents Floatzel from drowning even in stormy seas. One might glimpse this species around fishing hamlets from time to time.
Species_froslass_Description: A Pokémon inhabited by the soul of a woman who died bearing a grudge in the snowy mountains. Legends of Froslass placing deathly curses on misbehaving men send shivers down my spine.
Species_gabite_Description: Though Gabite are usually of a violent disposition, when I gave one a glass bead it had been eyeing covetously, it suddenly became quite docile.
Species_gallade_Description: Upon its evolution, Gallade has quite literally sharpened its psychokinetic energy into blades. It is a master of swordsmanship and chivalry, using its telepathic capabilities to sense those that need its protection. If the situation calls for it, Gallade will fight with cunning and savage tactics. Just by closing its eyes, it can effortlessly glance into the future to predict its opponents' moves, and counter with a blindingly fast strike from the blades on its elbows.
Species_garchomp_Description: Soars across the heavens at blinding speed—a magnificent sight! It has a feral disposition. Utmost caution is required if one meets a Garchomp out in the wilds.
Species_gastrodon_Description: Eats beach sand for nourishment. Should one Gastrodon encounter another of a different color, a fierce battle will inevitably ensue.
Species_gible_Description: It nests in caves untouched by sunlight. Its sharp teeth may fall out when worn away or after an impact, but they regrow within a few days.
Species_giratina_Description: There is one Hisuian verse that tells of a powerful light creating a deep shadow. I imagine that this deep shadow is Giratina.
Species_glaceon_Description: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.
Species_glameow_Description: Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.
Species_gliscor_Description: It glides soundlessly on pitch-black wings and sinks sharp fangs into the throat of its prey. It takes on a look of satisfaction once it has entirely drained its prey of blood.
Species_grotle_Description: Appears where there is clean spring water. The fruit that grows on the shrubs on its shell is sweet, nutritious, and truly delicious.
Species_happiny_Description: In imitation of Chansey, it keeps a round stone tucked into its belly pouch and cherishes it dearly. It gets along well with children and will sometimes play house with them for fun.
Species_heatran_Description: Stories tell of this Pokémon being birthed from the boiling magma within Mount Coronet. Its molten-steel body holds many mysteries.
Species_hippopotas_Description: Though large and languid, Hippopotas is difficult to detect due to its tendency to burrow into and lurk beneath the soil. When agitated or excited, it expels sand from its nostrils.
Species_hippowdon_Description: Short-tempered and easily moved to violence. It whips up whirlwinds of sand to crush its foes' spirits, then goes in for the attack.
Species_honchkrow_Description: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.
Species_infernape_Description: A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.
Species_kricketot_Description: When the trees take on new hues, more of these Pokémon appear. The tone they create by striking their antennae together resembles that of the marimba, an instrument of foreign lands.
Species_kricketune_Description: It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.
Species_leafeon_Description: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.
Species_lickilicky_Description: Its tongue can extend and contract freely, and it is capable of reaching lengths over 10 times Lickilicky's height. Beware of the saliva, as it contains corrosive elements.
Species_lopunny_Description: Its fur is warm and yet remarkably light. This Pokémon kicks as though it were a master of karate, driving back its opponents with ease.
Species_lucario_Description: A most gallant-looking creature. It emits energy waves and controls them with precision, using them to sense even faraway beings. I have given the name ”aura” to this power.
Species_lumineon_Description: Uses its gleaming fins to hunt its prey. The view of Lumineon schooling near the surface of the sea at night is breathtaking— it's as though there were shining stars right there.
Species_luxio_Description: The scratches from this Pokémon's claws can deliver severe shocks, potentially causing paralysis in the affected limbs. Despite Luxio's active and daring attitude, it also has easy-going moments, particularly at night when it snuggles up with other members of its pride. They form pairs and intertwine their tails, sharing and transferring the electricity they’ve accumulated throughout the day.
Species_luxray_Description: When Luxray's eyes light up, it gains the ability to see through walls and surfaces, regardless of thickness. This power allows it to easily spot any hiding prey, significantly increasing its hunting success rate. Contrary to what its fearsome appearance and abilities might suggest, Luxray is actually a family-oriented Pokémon, devoted to protecting, teaching, and entertaining the members of its pride. In fact, males at the top of the hierarchy sometimes go hungry to ensure that all other members, including those at the bottom, don’t miss a meal.
Species_magmortar_Description: Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.
Species_magnezone_Description: I theorize that a special magnetic field influenced this Pokémon, changing its molecular structure and causing it to evolve. It emits strange radio waves toward space from its antenna.
Species_mamoswine_Description: This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.
Species_manaphy_Description: Rumored to migrate across the oceans and visit Hisui's coastal waters only rarely. Although Manaphy resembles Phione, it is also quite different. The relation between the two is unclear.
Species_mantyke_Description: Though ball-like in shape, this Pokémon is a proficient swimmer. I have discovered that if a Mantyke spends much time with schools of Remoraid, it will eventually achieve evolution.
Species_mesprit_Description: Known as the Being of Emotion. In legend, this Pokémon was feared, as any who showed disrespect would have their emotions thrown into disarray.
Species_mime-jr_Description: Known to turn up in bustling marketplaces now and again. It mimics people much as a child would, then watches how they react, eyes sparkling.
Species_mismagius_Description: Mismagius can often be found in warped forests, where its mystic capabilities are heightened in the presence of so many Endermen. In this environment especially, it's best to stay in this Pokémon's good graces. While Mismagius can perform incantations to ward off misfortune and bring happiness, it can just as easily work curses to bring disaster to you if it becomes displeased.
Species_monferno_Description: The deeper the blue on its face, the more powerful it will grow to become. It leaps about every which way and lands powerful blows against its opponents with the flame on its tail.
Species_mothim_Description: Scatters steel-colored scales as it flaps its wings. Despite being observed feeding primarily on the nectar of flowers, Mothim is not often seen around flower gardens.
Species_munchlax_Description: Its robust stomach allows it to nonchalantly devour even rotted matter. It pays frequent visits to villages, seeking out food scraps intended for compost.
Species_pachirisu_Description: A species related to the Pikachu line. Though Pachirisu is a calm Pokémon, it still presents a danger should one touch its electrified tail or cheeks.
Species_palkia_Description: This Pokémon is feared as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Palkia was what caused the walls of our world to disappear, creating a sky that spans for infinity.
Species_phione_Description: Can be seen floating offshore during seasons when the seas are warm. Its azure body blends in with the ocean waters—logic suggests this is a defense mechanism against natural predators.
Species_piplup_Description: Prefers cold climes and appears along coasts. It's an adorable little thing—as cute as any child—but it's also prideful, unwilling to accept handouts from people.
Species_porygon-z_Description: Something has gone horribly, horribly wrong. Another bizarre item of dubious origin was used to evolve this Pokémon, but the result just seems... incorrect. Make no mistake, this is an upgrade; Porygon-Z is in every way stronger than both of its predecessors, but the haphazardness in its behavior and its erratic movement are highly concerning. It doesn't seem to be in pain, but it should go without saying that extra-dimensional travel is no longer a consideration.
Species_prinplup_Description: It swims gracefully through the frigid sea and sings with a voice like the roaring tide. It has powerful, sturdy wings and dignity to match.
Species_probopass_Description: Exposure to a powerful source of magnetism has caused Nosepass to evolve into this Pokémon, giving it newfound control over its own magnetic field. By manipulating the forces of attraction and repulsion, Probopass skillfully directs its three mini-noses to attack in battle. Its magnetic field is so powerful that appliances like PCs and Healing Machines are sometimes known to deactivate in its presence.
Species_purugly_Description: Though impudent and difficult to tame, Purugly enjoys great popularity due to its fur, the beauty of which surpasses even velveteen.
Species_rampardos_Description: Very little is known about its biology. Can knock down massive trees by smashing its beautiful, pearl-like crown against them.
Species_regigigas_Description: According to legend, Regigigas pulled landmasses together and bound them with rope to create the continent of Hisui. Though I have my doubts, the story could well contain a shred of truth.
Species_rhyperior_Description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.
Species_riolu_Description: Though infantile in appearance, it has the mysterious ability to read the minds of humans. The pure of heart are met with Riolu's approval, while those of ill nature earn only its loathing.
Species_roserade_Description: Hidden within the bouquet on each hand are thorned whips loaded with virulent poison. Roserade moves gracefully as it corners its prey and mercilessly lashes them with its whips.
Species_rotom_Description: This bizarre Pokémon appears to be a will-o'-the-wisp powered by electricity. Be wary, as Rotom is both smart and mischievous.
Species_shaymin_Description: When the turning of seasons brings the cruel winter to its end and the joyous people give thanks to the heavens, Shaymin appears and covers the withered land with flowers.
Species_shellos_Description: Found in abundance on seashores bordering warm waters. Shellos are unexpectedly friendly and will crawl toward any person they see. Take care not to get coated in mucus!
Species_shieldon_Description: Much remains unknown about this Pokémon, as few have ever seen it. However, we know that it is calm and dislikes conflict, and it enjoys polishing its face against trees and rocks.
Species_shinx_Description: The contractions of Shinx's muscles produce small amounts of electricity, which can be quickly released as light when it feels nervous or scared. This method of temporarily blinding its enemies provides Shinx with enough time to escape to safety. To build strength and courage, Shinx engage in playful brawls with other members of their pride, or even with Luxray, who hold back and feign defeat to boost the confidence of their young..
Species_skorupi_Description: Its claws are not only razor-sharp but poisonous, making Skorupi a highly dangerous Pokémon. It seems to be weakened by cold temperatures, however.
Species_skuntank_Description: Sprays a poisonous fluid to take down prey. Sometimes, unable to stomach the stench of its own fluid, it leaves the bested prey uneaten.
Species_snover_Description: One is likely to encounter this Pokémon while out in the snow. There are stories of Snover appearing in human settlements but doing no harm—rather, they bond with the children.
Species_spiritomb_Description: Legend has it that Spiritomb is the product of 108 malevolent spirits that were bound to an Odd Keystone due to their misdeeds centuries ago. These spirits retain a will of their own and unite in their quest for revenge. When they cannot locate the one who cursed them, they turn to other victims, seeking to unleash the anguish they've amassed over the ages. With a mere thought, they can cast wicked and mischievous curses upon anyone who passes their gaze.
Species_staraptor_Description: It has left the flock, having gained strength enough to survive on its own. The astounding force with which Staraptor flies through the air allows it to carry away large, burly targets.
Species_staravia_Description: They form remarkably large flocks and are constantly fighting amongst themselves. I suspect that those with magnificent plumes on their heads are the strong ones.
Species_starly_Description: They live in the fields and mountains, gathering in large flocks. Their cries are quite obnoxious. Though small, their wings are strong—a strike from them leaves pain that persists for a week.
Species_stunky_Description: The poison that gushes from its aft end is accompanied by an utterly evil-smelling odor with such potency that one whiff can induce memory loss.
Species_tangrowth_Description: The vines tipped in red are much more durable than the rest, so Tangrowth swings them around and ensnares prey with them as though they were arms. These vines grow especially quickly, and can grow back in seconds if they're cut off. When foxes attempt to search its body for berries, it gets sent into a frenzy, and it will use its "arms" to throw the poor critters, sometimes entire biomes away.
Species_togekiss_Description: Scant few have ever sighted this Pokémon. After studying what literature remains, I am certain Togekiss will reveal itself when peace reigns in the land.
Species_torterra_Description: This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.
Species_toxicroak_Description: Its crimson claws contain a virulent toxin. This toxin can be made into a tonic by diluting it, mixing it with several types of wild grass, and boiling it down over two days.
Species_turtwig_Description: This Pokémon becomes more energetic the more sunlight there is. The part resembling a shell is similar to silt and is slightly damp and warm to the touch.
Species_uxie_Description: A Pokémon feared but also respected for stealing away the memories of evildoers. I have found records that suggest Uxie holds dominion over knowledge.
Species_vespiquen_Description: Commands its subjects to build its hive. It will dispatch any interlopers who dare sneak into its nest and use them as nourishment for itself.
Species_weavile_Description: Evolution has not only enhanced this Pokémon's physical strength but also its cunning intellect. With razor-sharp claws and clever tactics, a pack of three to five Weavile can easily deceive other Pokémon into ambushes. This species appears to have even developed a primitive language, scrawling markings on trees and stones to communicate with others in their pack.
Species_wormadam_Description: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon's body. The cloak is never shed.
